key_safety.text: In JUPITER-02 (combination), most common adverse reactions (≥20%) included nausea (71%), vomiting (68%), decreased appetite (55%), hypothyroidism (38%); serious adverse reactions occurred in 43%. In POLARIS-02 (single agent), most common adverse reactions included hypothyroidism (27%), fatigue (22%), and cough (20%); serious adverse reactions occurred in 24% and fatal adverse reactions in 3.7%. Immune-related adverse events and infusion-related reactions were the significant identified safety issues.

requirement.text: 4471-1 Conduct a clinical trial enrolling a total sample size of 100 patients in the United States (U.S.) and Canada, that includes a sufficient representation of patients in racial and ethnic minority subgroups and is reflective of the U.S. population of patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), to further characterize the safety and efficacy of toripalimab in combination with cisplatin and gemcitabine in these patients. Include a sufficient number of patients with the keratinizing subtype reflecting the incidence of keratinizing NPC in the U.S. population. Conduct sparse sampling for supportive population pharmacokinetic and Exposure-Response (E-R) analyses. The E-R analyses may be used as supportive evidence for the efficacy and safety in the intended patient population. In the E-R analyses report, include an analysis of the presence and clinical impact of the neutralizing anti-drug antibodies on pharmacokinetics, efficacy and safety of toripalimab.
